requirement:
Each public SDK item has one defining module path. The SDK exposes no public
re-exports. The chapter that introduces each supported type or free function owns its declaration.
The [public API inventory](sdk/public-api.md) links each item to that requirement,
which describes its purpose
and declares its public Rust interface, including fields, enum variants, trait
members, and inherent methods. A change to that interface requires a change to
the owning requirement. Every supported struct with public fields is
`#[non_exhaustive]`. Its constructor accepts the values needed to create it.
Additional fields have consuming builder methods that accept a concrete value.
Optional fields start as `None`. Backend inference options start empty and can
be added one key at a time.

The SDK’s public modules follow the interfaces introduced in these chapters.

- `domain`: application data and the `Domain` and `NodeContents` traits.
- `graph`: criterion definitions, graph observations, evidence, and functions for running criteria.
- `request`: `ValidationContext`, typed `Ask` builders, context values, and request phases.
- `agent`: configuration for the supplied agents.
- `sources`: project inspection, search queries, and their results.
- `outline`: selectable source contents and language rules; `outline::languages`
  supplies bundled languages, and `outline::selector` defines selector syntax.
- `storage`: filesystem evidence storage.

Source access, search engines, redaction, provider transports, agent-result paging,
and conversation machinery are implementation details of those interfaces.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.sdk.public_api`. I did not run the tests. I read the test source and helpers listed below.

**Structural obligations**
- **No public re-exports.** `tests/public_api.rs#fn[sdk_has_no_public_reexports]` parses every `.rs` file under `src` with tree-sitter and fails on any `use_declaration` with a plain `pub` visibility. `pub(crate)` imports are correctly allowed.
- **One defining module path per item.** `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` walks the rustdoc HTML module tree from the crate root and asserts there are no "Duplicate rustdoc export" entries. Together with the re-export ban, this covers the single-path rule.
- **Module set and inventory.** The same test compares the rustdoc exports (paths and item kinds) with the inventory parsed from `md/requirements/sdk`. It reports both missing and unexpected items.
- **No Cargo features.** The same test asserts that the crate defines none.
- **Hidden items.** Its helper `check_hidden_exports` rejects `#[doc(hidden)]` public items. Rustdoc would omit these, so the check closes a loophole in the export comparison.
- **Owning requirement declares the full interface, and an interface change needs a requirement change.** `check_declaration`, reached from `public_exports_match_the_appendix` through `documented_exports`, does four things for each exported item:
  - It requires a description and a Rust declaration in the owning requirement.
  - It compares the declared signatures with rustdoc, with fields, enum variants, methods and trait impls all included. It fails on differences in either direction.
  - It compares the indexed member names.
  - It compares the declared trait impls.
- **Signature comparison is itself tested.** `fn[member_order_is_free_but_field_and_method_types_are_committed]` shows that member order is irrelevant. It also shows that changing a field type, a return type, or `&mut self` versus `&self` is detected, and that `(T,)` differs from `(T)`.
- **Every struct with public fields is `#[non_exhaustive]`.** `check_declaration` asserts `#[non_exhaustive]` in the rustdoc declaration for each exported struct that has `structfield` entries.

**Constructor, builder and default obligations** (behavioural tests marked `requirements.sdk.public_api`)
- **Backend configs.** `src/agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` covers `BedrockConfig`, `OpenAiConfig`, `OllamaConfig` and `BedrockCredentials`:
  - Constructors with only the required values serialize to just those fields, so optional fields start as `None`.
  - Every consuming builder is exercised: `aws_profile`, `region`, `credentials`, `session_token`, `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key`.
  - `options` starts empty and gains one key per `option` call. A repeated key is overwritten.
  - Assertions are on exact serialized JSON.
- **Outline types.** `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` covers `OutlineItem`, `Outline` and `OutlineAttachment`. It checks that `name_span`, `header_span`, `trailer_span` and `diagnostic` start empty, that the constructor keeps its values, and that each builder sets its field.
- **Selector types.** `src/outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` covers `Segment`. `ordinal` starts as `None`, and the `ordinal` builder and `SelectorError::new` are exercised.
- **Source types.** `tests/source_defaults.rs` has three marked tests. `fn[source_bytes_error_kinds_and_language_names_round_trip]` covers `SourceFile`: `language` starts as `None` and the `language` builder sets it. `fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` covers `TextQuery`: `limit` is `None` and `context_lines` is `0` by default, and the `scope`, `context_lines` and `limit` builders work. `fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]` covers `StructuralQuery`: `limit` is `None` by default and the `scope` and `limit` builders work.

**Other structs.** Some other non-exhaustive structs have public fields and no optional fields: `Fingerprint`, `Snapshot`, `Span`, `OutlineData`, `OutlineError`, `UsageStats`, `ToolUsage`, `TokenCount`, `TextMatch`, `StructuralMatch`, `SearchResults`, `SearchHit` and `Record`.
- Their constructors only take the required values and pass them through, so there is no default or builder behaviour to test.
- The signature check against the declared interface covers whether the constructors exist and take the right types.

The `{test}` references on the sample tests name `requirements.sdk.public_api`. The assertions are behavioural and match the requirement text.
